## ✨ Added

- A clean, self-hosted file sharer for Unraid with no logins: open the page, drop a file, set an expiry, share the link. There are no accounts and no heavy stack behind it.
- One-page upload: a central drop zone. Drop a file and a settings panel slides in on the right with the expiry and an optional password. Upload progress shows as an overlay right on the drop zone. A light/dark toggle sits in the header.
- Resumable uploads (tus): multi-GB files survive connection drops and pick up where they left off.
- Per-share expiry: 1 hour, 6 hours, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, or never. A background job removes expired files and their metadata.
- Optional password, hashed with scrypt and never stored in plain text. Once the password checks out, the download streams natively. The permission cookie is derived from the server-only hash, so nobody can forge it from the public link.
- Share page with a copyable link and a QR code for phones.
- Easy to set up on Unraid: add the template, map `/data` to your appdata and pick a port. Behind a reverse proxy, set `BASE_URL` (for example `https://share.yourdomain.tld`) so share links use your public domain. `MAX_FILE_SIZE` (bytes, 0 = unlimited) and `DEFAULT_EXPIRY` are optional.

## 🎨 Design

- Gold feather logo: a flowing feather with a light to metallic to deep gold gradient. It is an inline SVG, so it stays crisp at any size in the header, on the download page and on the not-found page. The source art is in `.github/assets/featherdrop-logo.svg`.
- Template icon: a 512×512 `icon.png` rendered from the logo, used as the Unraid Community Applications template icon.
- White banner: the white `#ffffff` 1600×500 README card with the gold feather centered and no text. The wordmark lives in the heading, and the README hero runs in the usual order: centered `<h1>`, tagline, banner, badge row, description.
- `scripts/render-assets.mjs` renders the banner and the icon from the logo SVG and centers the feather by its real bounding box. It pulls in `@resvg/resvg-js` on demand, so it isn't a project dependency.

## ⚡ Improved

- Architecture: one container running Next.js (App Router) with Mantine UI, plus a small custom Node server that mounts the tus upload handler next to Next. Files live on a local volume and metadata sits in one SQLite file (`better-sqlite3`), so there is no database server and no login system.
- CI opts into Node 24: the workflows set `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24` ahead of GitHub's forced switch on 2026-06-16, which clears the Node 20 deprecation warning on the checkout and Docker actions.
- A much simpler take inspired by Pingvin Share: no backend stack, no accounts, you just drop a file and share it.
